options: A reusable, stored metric computed over data model objects
A visual chart placed on a dashboard
A connection that ingests a source system
A rule that merges duplicate people
questions.explain: A calculated insight is a governed aggregate, such as lifetime value, stored as its own queryable object so it can be reused.

questions.q: Which option on the New Calculated Insight screen computes metrics from real-time data sources?
options: Create with Builder
Create with SQL
Create Streaming Insights
Create from a Package
questions.explain: Create Streaming Insights is for metrics computed across dimensions from real-time sources; the other options are the builder, SQL, and installed packages.

questions.q: In a calculated insight, what does a dimension do?
options: It holds the aggregated number, such as a sum
It is the attribute you group by, which sets the grain of the result
It schedules how often the insight refreshes
It deletes rows that fail the WHERE clause
questions.explain: Measures are aggregated values; dimensions are the grouping attributes. Together they define the grain.

questions.q: Why do organizations define metrics like lifetime value as calculated insights?
options: Because dashboards cannot calculate anything themselves
Because it removes the need for data streams
Because it guarantees the metric is legally compliant
So one consistent definition is reused instead of each team rebuilding it differently
questions.explain: Central definitions prevent conflicting numbers across dashboards. Privacy compliance still needs human review.

questions.q: What warning appears in the calculated insight SQL editor?
options: The SQL will run only once
A calculated insight can affect data protection and privacy compliance
GROUP BY is not supported
Only administrators can write SELECT statements
questions.explain: Metrics derived from personal data can still affect privacy compliance, so governance owners should be involved when in doubt.
